baseline.description: No change: keep the current setup
baseline.variant_facts:
The merchandise under consideration is a Item 10364-SF, Stack Chair 14. A single-person metal and plastic stacking seat without upholstery or armrests. It consists of stainless steel metal legs affixed to a unitary polyolefin plastic seat foundation and backrest shell, along with glides, washers, rivets, glue, labels, and packaging. The Item 10364-SF, Stack Chair 14 is assembled in Mexico using components sourced from China, United States, Portugal and Mexico.

The Stainless steel metal leg assembly, Leg post swivel glides, Washers and Rivets are produced in China. The Polyolefin plastic seat foundation and backrest shell, Corrugated fanfold and US labels are sourced from United States. The Glue are sourced from Portugal. The Local labels are produced in Mexico. 

Final assembly in Mexico: Affix unitary plastic seat foundation and backrest shell to stainless steel metal legs; Assemble incomplete, unassembled, and unfinished seating components with glides, washers, rivets, and glue; Inspect and package finished stacking chair with labels and corrugated fanfold.

prediction.decisive_step: Manufacturing of the stainless steel metal leg assembly in China
prediction.reasoning: The assembly in Mexico—affixing a pre-formed US plastic shell to a pre-fabricated Chinese metal leg frame using rivets, washers, glides, and glue—is a simple assembly operation that does not result in a substantial transformation. Under CBP precedent for metal-framed seating, when simple assembly does not confer origin, the structural metal frame/leg assembly imparts the essential character and structural support to the chair, making China the country of origin.

key_factors: Unitary polyolefin plastic seat foundation/backrest shell and stainless steel leg assembly
prediction.decisive_step: Manufacturing of the plastic seat shell and metal leg assembly in China
prediction.reasoning: The essential character of the stacking chair is imparted by its primary structural components: the unitary plastic seat/backrest shell and the stainless steel leg assembly, both entirely produced in China. Under CBP precedent, simple assembly of pre-fabricated furniture components using rivets, washers, glides, and glue does not constitute a substantial transformation. Because the Mexican operations are mere simple assembly and packaging of components whose form and use are predetermined in China, the country of origin remains China.

verdict.reasoning: In Variant A, CBP determined the origin was the United States because the simple assembly in Mexico of affixing the unitary polyolefin plastic seat foundation and backrest shell (from the US) to the stainless steel legs (from China) did not result in a substantial transformation, and the US-origin seat and backrest shell imparted the essential character of the chair. In Variant B, production of the polyolefin plastic seat foundation and backrest shell moves to China. With both the seat/backrest shell and the metal leg assembly made in China, the country of origin shifts to China.
